newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds stable to lower, seen inactive.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds stable to lower, seen inactive.

text.p: Argentine bonds were stable to slightly lower Friday in late morning trade as the market found little motivation to move.
"There is a pause in the market, but it is stable at a very high level which shows its firmness," said a trader at a foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slipped $0.10 to 120.60, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 was flat at 84-3/4.
The trader said he expected the market to tread water this session in absence of any anticipated market-moving news.
The market was hampered by a slow U.S. Treasury market. In addition, the gaining view that shares are cheap compared with bonds could hold the market back in coming days.
Analysts at financial consultancy IDEA said in an investor note that "the ratio between equity-bond yield ratios are starting to act as a restraining factor" for bonds.
